baseline_retrieval.text: Atorvastatin (a statin) and aspirin are frequently co-administered for the secondary prevention of cardiovascular events. No clinically significant pharmacokinetic drug-drug interactions have been observed when atorvastatin is co-administered with aspirin.

Co-administration of warfarin and aspirin significantly increases the risk of major gastrointestinal and intracranial bleeding. Combination therapy requires close INR monitoring and risk-benefit evaluation.
Combining haloperidol with azithromycin causes additive QTc interval prolongation, increasing the risk of life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias including Torsades de Pointes.

Spironolactone can cause severe hyperkalemia, which can lead to cardiac arrhythmias and sudden death. Concomitant administration with potassium supplements or potassium-sparing diuretics is strictly contraindicated.
Metformin decreases hepatic glucose production, decreases intestinal absorption of glucose, and improves insulin sensitivity by increasing peripheral glucose uptake and utilization.
